analysis.subject: biology
analysis.pageCoverage: The page explains random mating as a condition for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and contrasts positive and negative assortative mating and their effects on homozygotes and heterozygotes in humans.

overview.headline: How random and assortative mating affect human genetics

keyPoints.point: A condition for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is random mating, which does not always occur in humans.
keyPoints.quote: One reason that Hardy-Weinberg does not always apply to humans is that random mating, a condition of HWE (Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium), does not occur.

keyPoints.point: Random mating means mating is arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.
keyPoints.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyPoints.point: Humans tend to mate with similar individuals for visible traits such as height and ethnicity.
keyPoints.quote: humans tend to mate with individuals that are similar to themselves

keyPoints.point: Positive assortative mating increases homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating increases heterozygotes.
keyPoints.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyPoints.point: Humans mate randomly for blood type and short tandem repeat genotype even though they mate assortatively for physical attributes.
keyPoints.quote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype

keyTerms.gloss: mating that is arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered
keyTerms.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyTerms.gloss: non-random mating between similar individuals that increases homozygotes
keyTerms.quote: This constitutes non-random, positive assortative mating.

keyTerms.gloss: breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes
keyTerms.quote: In contrast, negative assortative mating is breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes, and is more rare.

keyTerms.gloss: genotypes with identical alleles that show an increase after positive assortative mating
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: genotypes with different alleles that show an increase after negative assortative mating
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: repeated DNA trait that is an example of randomly mating traits such as blood type
keyTerms.quote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype

componentPlan.focusQuote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Quiz cards give quick checks of definitions and effects for random and assortative mating
